result.rationale: The diff shows TopicEmbed.import_remote passes `tags: %w[div p code pre h1 h2 h3 b em i strong a img], attributes: %w[href src]` to Readability, so anchor hrefs (including `javascript:` scheme URLs) survive. Post#cook then does `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline entirely, and the imported HTML is rendered as-is (later displayed via `raw post.cooked`). So malicious script URLs in fetched content are stored and served unsanitized — a real security defect introduced by this diff.

record.issue_text: In the import_remote/readability path, href is preserved by the tag whitelist so javascript: URLs survive sanitization

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, `Readability::Document.new` is configured to keep `<a>` tags and preserve the `href` attribute (`tags: ... a ...`, `attributes: %w[href src]`). The extracted `doc.content` is then imported via `TopicEmbed.import`, which creates a post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. `Post#cook` returns `raw` verbatim for `raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline, and the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. Therefore a `javascript:` URL in an imported `<a href>` would be persisted and output as-is, creating an XSS/unsafe link vector in the embed content.
